```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Lower friction to a first sale within 90 days. A sells a one-off or monthly research document to an individual who can expense or self-fund it. Foray's $60/blueprint anchor shows a single-transaction purchase exists. B sells software that sits inside a production execution path, and the brief says buyers in that space already expect SOC 2, GDPR/DPA and EU AI Act evidence packs. A six-week solo build cannot produce those.",
    "B's trust barrier is structural, not cosmetic. The brief names trust in a one-person vendor for destructive-action gating as a high bar. A's trust problem is real too: Gixo says a human must verify every number. But a buyer can still pay for a draft they verify themselves. Nobody pays for a safety gate they don't trust.",
    "Free substitutes hurt B more. B lists fully free OSS options (agent-safety-layer, plus free tiers at SealGate, Retrace, OpenGuardrails, Exogram and Sekuire's SDK) across nine-plus competitors. A's five competitors all charge, from Gixo's $10/mo workspace to Foray's $299/mo, which signals that paid demand is not yet fully commoditized.",
    "No regulatory setup stands between A and a first invoice. B's brief explicitly flags DPA, GDPR and SOC 2 Type II as immediately relevant or de facto required in the category."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence shows fear of the problem, not willingness to pay a third party to solve it. The r/LLMDevs quote ('terrified of integrating agents') expresses anxiety, not intent to buy. The r/AI_Agents quote comes from someone who builds agents for a living and lists HITL controls as what makes a good agent, which reads as building it in-house. The PocketOS incident is a single anecdote. Nothing in the brief shows a team paying an unproven vendor when free OSS alternatives exist.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence; both briefs are thin and both ideas sit in crowded niches. A's own evidence is weak. One demand quote ('the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can') arguably argues against a tool. Paid acquisition (~$104 CPL) is poor against a ~$60 price. The open question of users defaulting to a general LLM chat is unanswered. B has stronger evidence that the pain is real and a cheaper launch channel (Show HN). The pick rests mainly on B's compliance and trust barriers, which matter most under a 90-day first-customer constraint."
}
```
